name: Guardian genius crossword No 193
preamble: The solutions for one lot of clues have a common theme, not further defined. All other clues contain a letter to be disregarded in order to reach their solutions. In clue order, these discarded letters spell out the theme of the first lot of solutions.

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One that sticks around looking gloomy

indicators.note: one thing placed around another wraps it, so the second piece sits inside the first

blocks.note: a gorer is an animal that sticks its horns into people
dim means dark or gloomy

explanation.surface: A miserable hanger-on who never leaves, wearing a sullen face.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed clue: there is no definition, only wordplay. Nadine Gordimer, the South African novelist, won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1991.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble's theme is Nobel laureates, and Nadine Gordimer received the literature prize in 1991.

clue.text: Alien man’s leg is a source of light

definitions.note: a verb phrase, matching the third-person verb

indicators.note: something alien is strange and foreign, so these letters take an unfamiliar order

blocks.note: the N of man's is the letter to discard; the rest is taken as written

explanation.surface: A sci-fi image: an extraterrestrial whose leg glows in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: Discard the N of man's, the first letter of NOBEL LAUREATES, then rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that gleams shines or glints, so it gives off light as a lamp or star does.

clue.text: Stop producing rehearsal after first half droops completely

indicators.note: with its extra O gone, the first half drops right down to the bottom, so it moves behind the second half

blocks.note: a dry run is a practice or rehearsal

explanation.surface: A theatre run in trouble: the dress rehearsal sags, and the show stops partway through.
explanation.walkthrough: Discard the O of droops, leaving drops. In a down entry the first word of the phrase drops to the foot, so the two halves swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: A well or a cow that runs dry has stopped yielding anything, so it no longer produces.

clue.text: Divine right finally beaten by northerners

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it
with its extra B discarded this reads eaten by, and what is eaten goes inside the eater

blocks.note: the Inuit are peoples of the Arctic north
its closing letter

explanation.surface: The divine right of kings has been overturned by people from the North.
explanation.walkthrough: Discard the B of beaten, leaving eaten. Divine is a verb here, not the adjective of divine right.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine something is to perceive it by insight, which is exactly what intuiting means.

clue.text: Aide loiters around leaders

indicators.note: letters turned around are moved about, so they are put into a new order

blocks.note: with one E discarded, Aide reads aid; the rest is taken as written

explanation.surface: An assistant hangs about the bosses, hoping to be noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: Discard an E from Aide. Leaders here are newspaper leading articles, not bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: In British newspapers a leader is the editorial column, giving the paper's own view on a story.

clue.text: Estate car’s right-hand side gets clipped

indicators.note: something clipped has had a part trimmed off, here the named half of the word

blocks.note: an estate is a holding of land
an auto is a car; its right-hand half is the part to be cut

explanation.surface: An estate car has scraped its offside panels against something.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed clue with no definition. The right-hand half of AUTO, its last two letters, is clipped, leaving AU. Lev Landau won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1962.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet physicist Lev Landau is a Nobel laureate, honoured in 1962 for his theory of liquid helium.

clue.text: Tissue’s wrongly diagnosed after black part of lung is removed

definitions.note: the clue's singular tissue for a plural answer; adenoids are a mass of tissue

indicators.note: with its extra L discarded, black reads back, so the back of the word is the part in question
removed means taken out, so that letter leaves the fodder
done wrongly means not in the proper order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
its back letter, the one to remove

explanation.surface: A medical blunder: tissue misread as a black spot on the lung.
explanation.walkthrough: Discard the L of black, leaving back: the back of lung is G, taken out of diagnosed before rearranging. Only one of deletion's two signals is needed; both name the same step.
explanation.definitionFit: Adenoids are a mass of lymphoid tissue at the back of the nose, so they are tissue.

clue.text: Hip stylist’s lending charlady clothes with style and grace

indicators.note: with its extra L discarded, lending reads ending, so the last letter is kept
clothes is a verb here: the cleaner dresses the other pieces, wrapping round them

blocks.note: a daily is a cleaning woman who comes in each day
in means fashionable, hip
its closing letter

explanation.surface: A trendy hairdresser lends the cleaner some elegant outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: Discard the L of lending. A charlady, or daily, is a British cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something daintily means doing it delicately and elegantly, with refinement and poise.

clue.text: Uranium ore lit unusual reactor below the surface

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so these letters are out of order

blocks.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium
taken as written
with its A discarded this reads rector, abbreviated R

explanation.surface: Nuclear fuel fires up a strange reactor deep underground.
explanation.walkthrough: Discard the A of reactor, leaving rector, a parish priest, whose abbreviation is R.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulterior motive is concealed, lying beneath what is openly shown, so it is hidden from view.

clue.text: Leading home network provider coming round this month

indicators.note: coming round something means encircling it, so one piece is wrapped about the other
leading means going in front, so this piece is placed before the word for home

blocks.note: EE is a British mobile phone network
inst, for instant, is the old commercial abbreviation for this month
at home is in

explanation.surface: An advert: the top broadband supplier is coming to your area this month.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed clue with no definition; the provider wrapped around this month leads home. Albert Einstein won the Nobel Prize in Physics for 1921.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein is a Nobel laureate, given the physics prize for explaining the photoelectric effect.

clue.text: Left musical without seeing finale by tenor

indicators.note: not seeing the finale means the show stops short of its final letter

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical about Eva Perón
T is the abbreviation for tenor

explanation.surface: Someone walked out of a show before the end, standing beside a singer.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed clue with no definition. Michael Levitt shared the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2013.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Levitt is a Nobel laureate, sharing the 2013 chemistry award for computer models of molecules.

clue.text: Exhibit behind screens starts to reveal royal lives

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept
a screen hides what is behind it, so the outer word encloses the inner pieces

blocks.note: to moon is to show one's bare backside
first letters of these two words
lives means exists, is

explanation.surface: A tabloid exposé: a hidden exhibit uncovers how a royal really lives.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed clue with no definition. Exhibit behind is not a museum piece: it means bare one's bottom. Toni Morrison won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1993.
explanation.definitionFit: Toni Morrison, the American novelist of Beloved, is a Nobel laureate, receiving the 1993 literature prize.

clue.text: Journalist loses heart from stress

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so only its central letters are taken
losing something means it is taken away, so those letters leave the word

blocks.note: a reporter is a journalist
the two central letters of this six-letter word

explanation.surface: A burnt-out reporter, worn down by the pressure of the job.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed clue with no definition. George Porter shared the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1967 for flash photolysis.
explanation.definitionFit: George Porter is a Nobel laureate, sharing the 1967 chemistry prize for studying very fast reactions.

clue.text: Historic document promoted cause of abstract artist to preserve school

indicators.note: with its U discarded this reads case, and a word's case is its outer shell of first and last letters
in a down entry, promoting moves things up, so the string reads from the bottom

blocks.note: its first and last letters
an RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
to can food is to preserve it in tins
a gam is a school of whales

explanation.surface: A treasured charter is used to advance the career of a modern painter by keeping an academy going.
explanation.walkthrough: Discard the U of cause. A gam is a herd or school of whales, a word from whaling days.
explanation.definitionFit: Magna Carta is the charter King John sealed in 1215, one of the most famous historic documents in England.

clue.text: River engulfing valley after current flowed

indicators.note: engulfing means swallowing whole, so the river's name surrounds the rest
after places the valley behind the earlier pieces in the sequence

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current
ran means flowed
a dell is a small wooded valley
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A flood: the river swamped the valley once the current surged.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed clue with no definition. Luigi Pirandello, Italian dramatist of Six Characters in Search of an Author, won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1934.
explanation.definitionFit: Luigi Pirandello is a Nobel laureate, the Italian playwright awarded the literature prize in 1934.

clue.text: Top brass repeatedly involved with liquidator

indicators.note: to top something is to cut its head off, so the first letter goes
repeatedly says the trimmed word appears twice in a row

blocks.note: with its R discarded this reads bass, before its head is cut off
involved in something is in it

explanation.surface: Senior officers keep getting entangled with someone winding up a failed company.
explanation.walkthrough: Discard the R of brass. A liquidator is not a company receiver here but one who liquidates, that is, kills.
explanation.definitionFit: To liquidate a person is slang for killing them, so a liquidator is a hired killer.

clue.text: Reset plastic surrounding shower screen

indicators.note: plastic material can be moulded into any shape, so these letters are reshaped
surrounding something means enclosing it, so the other piece sits inside

blocks.note: with one E discarded this reads rest
a shower is a spell of rain

explanation.surface: A DIY job: refitting the plastic trim round a shower screen.
explanation.walkthrough: Discard an E from Reset. Screen is a verb-like noun here: a sieve that screens out lumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A strainer is a sieve, which screens solids out of a liquid, so it is a kind of screen.

clue.text: A void gauche volunteers meeting chief in advance

indicators.note: a void word has had its inside emptied, so only its outer letters stay

blocks.note: its first and last letters
the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve
a head is a chief

explanation.surface: An awkward empty-headed volunteer meets the boss ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: Discard the opening A, which belongs to the hidden message rather than the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To get ahead is to make progress or succeed in life, so it means to advance.

clue.text: The lads run wild!

indicators.note: running wild means out of control, so these letters go every which way

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation as a gang of boys goes on the rampage.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed clue with no definition, just letters to rearrange. Earl Sutherland won the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1971 for work on hormones.
explanation.definitionFit: Earl Sutherland is a Nobel laureate, awarded the 1971 medicine prize for discovering how hormones act.

clue.text: Unmarried woman that raised triplets maddens nurses

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so only the letters cradled across the gap between the words are kept and the outer ones are dropped
in a down entry, raised means lifted upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: with its second T discarded this reads triples, and its last three letters are kept
its first three letters, carrying the run across the word break

explanation.surface: A spinster who brought up triplets, and the strain drives her mad.
explanation.walkthrough: A hidden word once the extra letter is gone: discard the second T of triplets, leaving triples, then read back through the letters straddling triples maddens.
explanation.definitionFit: Damsel is an old word for a young unmarried woman, as in the damsel in distress.

clue.text: Neighbour lied to judge in a murder case

definitions.note: a verb here, as in fields that neighbour the river, which matches the verb answer

indicators.note: in places the judge inside the phrase for a killing

blocks.note: the E of lied is the letter to discard; what remains has no part in the wordplay
taken as written
do in is slang for murder
J is the abbreviation for judge

explanation.surface: A neighbour gives false evidence to the judge in a murder trial.
explanation.walkthrough: The discarded E must come from lied, keeping NOBEL LAUREATES in order, but lid to then has no clear job; this parse leaves those words unexplained.
explanation.definitionFit: To neighbour something is to lie next to it, which is what adjoin means.

clue.text: Mutant strains in part of insect’s development

indicators.note: a mutant has been changed in form, so these letters change their order

blocks.note: with one S discarded this reads strain

explanation.surface: A lab note: altered genetic strains turn up at one stage of an insect's growth.
explanation.walkthrough: Discard an S from strains, the last letter of NOBEL LAUREATES.
explanation.definitionFit: An instar is a stage in an insect's growth between two moults of its outer skin.

clue.text: National service enriches apathetic adolescents’ training to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with points to the opening letter of each of the preceding words
something that enriches is put into the other thing, so it goes inside

blocks.note: opening letter
the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is one of Britain's armed services
opening letters

explanation.surface: A columnist argues that bringing back conscription would do lazy teenagers good.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed clue with no definition. Yasser Arafat shared the Nobel Peace Prize in 1994.
explanation.definitionFit: Yasser Arafat, the Palestinian leader, is a Nobel laureate, sharing the 1994 peace prize after the Oslo Accords.

clue.text: Host passing fancy retreat

blocks.note: an MC, master of ceremonies, hosts an event
a fad is a short-lived craze
a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: A party host with a sudden whim to hide away somewhere quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed clue with no definition. Daniel McFadden shared the Nobel Prize in Economics in 2000.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel McFadden is a Nobel laureate, sharing the 2000 economics prize for methods of analysing discrete choice.

clue.text: Drives round bend when cycling

indicators.note: letters cycling go round like a wheel, so the last one comes off the back and rides on at the front

blocks.note: to drive someone round the bend is to infuriate them

explanation.surface: A motorist or cyclist steers around a curve in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed clue with no definition. Round the bend is British for mad. Frederick Sanger won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry twice, in 1958 and 1980.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederick Sanger is a double Nobel laureate in chemistry, for sequencing insulin and then DNA.

clue.text: How one might describe Amundsen’s arrival at the South Pole?

blocks.clueFragment: How one might describe Amundsen’s arrival at the South Pole?
blocks.note: surface reading: an account of the Norwegian explorer reaching the Pole in December 1911

blocks.clueFragment: Amundsen’s arrival at the South Pole?
blocks.note: setter's reading: Amundsen got there before Robert Falcon Scott, so his arrival came ahead of the British party

explanation.surface: A history question about the race to the South Pole.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed clue with no definition: the answer splits as PRE (before) and SCOTT, the British explorer Amundsen beat to the Pole by five weeks. Edward Prescott shared the Nobel Prize in Economics in 2004.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Prescott is a Nobel laureate, sharing the 2004 economics prize for work on business cycles.

clue.text: Criminal under arrest giving away almost everything

indicators.note: giving away nearly all of the word leaves just its opening letter
criminal means crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
all but the opening letter is given away

explanation.surface: A detained suspect blabs, giving up nearly every secret to police.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed clue with no definition. Pablo Neruda, the Chilean poet, won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Neruda, the Chilean poet, is a Nobel laureate, receiving the literature prize in 1971.

clue.text: Football’s governing body meets new head of state about country hosting league

indicators.note: a host takes a guest in, so the country's letters hold the league's

blocks.note: the FA is the Football Association, which runs English football
the United Kingdom
L is the abbreviation for league
N is the abbreviation for new
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the British head of state

explanation.surface: The football authorities meet a new president to discuss a country staging a league.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed clue with no definition. ER is the Queen's cipher, Elizabeth Regina. William Faulkner won the Nobel Prize in Literature for 1949.
explanation.definitionFit: William Faulkner, the Mississippi novelist, is a Nobel laureate, receiving the literature prize for 1949.
